correctness.rationale: For Lebesgue binary digits the joint Shannon entropy of finite linear parity forms equals GF(2)-row rank. The first protocol is generated over GF(2)[s²] by p and s q: determinant nonzero yields independence at every finite horizon; determinant zero gives a nontrivial finite-degree syzygy and rank N+O(1). The second protocol is generated over GF(2)[s] by p,q, necessarily rank N+O(1). An exact parity-to-E_k factorization proves both pairwise-independent XOR examples and finite-block ranks. An exact finite checker tested 961 polynomial pairs at 3 block lengths, plus examples up to N=19; finite checks support but do not establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem is a complete classification for every pair of finite parity sensors under the two natural schedules posed in the 2024 paper. It gives an exact 1-versus-1/2 entropy-rate dichotomy and identifies a nontrivial failure of any pairwise-correlation test to detect an entropy loss, with explicit three-bit XOR witnesses. It distinguishes deterministic information flow from superficial single-sensor randomness; no unsupported cryptographic impact is asserted.
